p.src: Now, Xifeng and Baoyu returned home and greeted everyone. Baoyu first reported to Grandmother Jia that Qin Zhong wished to attend the family school. He said that he himself would then have a study companion and could apply himself in earnest, and he warmly praised Qin Zhong's character and conduct as exceptionally lovable. Xifeng supported him from the side, adding, among other things, that Qin Zhong would come in a few days to pay his respects to the Old Ancestress, and this delighted Grandmother Jia. Seizing the opportunity, Xifeng invited Grandmother Jia to come and see the opera the day after next. Though advanced in years, Grandmother Jia was exceedingly fond of such amusements. When the day came, Madam You also arrived to invite her, so Grandmother Jia took Lady Wang, Lin Daiyu, Baoyu, and the others with her to see the opera. At noon, Grandmother Jia returned to rest. Lady Wang was naturally fond of peace and quiet, so when she saw Grandmother Jia return, she came back as well. Xifeng then took the place of honor, and everyone enjoyed themselves until evening; nothing further need be said.

p.src: Now Baoyu, having escorted Grandmother Jia home and waited until she lay down for her midday nap, intended to return to the opera for more amusement. Yet he feared that his presence might inconvenience Madam Qin and the others. Then he remembered that Xue Baochai had lately been convalescing at home and that he had not yet called on her in person, so he decided to pay her a visit. If he went through the rear side gate of the principal apartments, he might be delayed by some other affair or, worse still, happen to meet his father. It would be better to take the longer way around. The nurses and maids were ready to help him change, but when they saw that he kept on the same clothes and went out through the second gate, they had no choice but to follow, still supposing that he was returning to the other mansion to see the opera. But on reaching the passage hall, he turned east and then north, making his way behind the reception hall. Just then he ran straight into two of his father's literary retainers, Zhan Guang and Shan Pinren. The moment they saw Baoyu, both hurried up laughing; one clasped him around the waist and the other took his hand, exclaiming, “Our blessed young master! I knew I must have had a lucky dream—it has taken us long enough to chance upon you!” With that, they bowed, exchanged greetings, and fussed over him for quite some time before at last moving away. An old nurse called them back and asked, “Have you two gentlemen just come from the Master's presence?” They nodded. “The Master is taking his midday nap in the small study at Dream Slope Studio. There is nothing to worry about.” They spoke as they walked away. Their words made Baoyu laugh as well. He then turned the corner and headed north toward Pear Fragrance Court. By chance, Wu Xindeng, chief steward of the silver treasury, Dai Liang, overseer of the granary, and several other supervisors—seven men in all—were coming out of the countinghouse. On seeing Baoyu, they hurried over and stood respectfully with their hands at their sides. One purchasing agent named Qian Hua, who had not seen Baoyu for many days, alone stepped briskly forward and sank to one knee in greeting. Baoyu smilingly took his hand and raised him up. They all said with a laugh, “The other day we saw some square calligraphy pieces written by Second Master. Your hand has improved wonderfully. When will you favor us with a few to hang up?” “Where did you see them?” Baoyu asked with a smile. “They are in several places,” they replied. “Everyone praises them to the skies and even asks us to obtain some.” Baoyu laughed. “They are nothing of value. Just tell my young attendants.” He continued walking as he spoke, and only after he had passed did the men disperse to their several duties.

p.src: Leaving idle matters aside, Baoyu arrived at Pear Fragrance Court and first entered Aunt Xue's room, where he found her sorting out needlework with her maids. Baoyu hastened to pay his respects. Aunt Xue at once took hold of him, drew him into her arms, and said with a smile, “My dear boy, on such a cold day, how thoughtful of you to come! Quickly, get up on the kang and sit down.” She ordered someone to bring piping-hot tea. Baoyu asked, “Is Cousin Xue not at home?” Aunt Xue sighed. “He is a horse without a bridle, forever rushing about. When would he ever consent to spend a whole day at home?” Baoyu said, “Has Cousin Baochai fully recovered?” “Yes, indeed,” said Aunt Xue. “And the other day you were thoughtful enough to send someone to inquire after her. She is in the inner room. Go and see her. It is warmer in there than here, so sit with her, and as soon as I have put these things in order, I will come in and talk with you.” Hearing this, Baoyu quickly got down from the kang and went to the door of the inner room, where he saw a somewhat worn red-silk curtain hanging. Baoyu lifted the curtain and stepped inside. At once he saw Xue Baochai seated on the kang doing needlework. Her glossy jet-black hair was gathered in a coil; she wore a honey-colored padded jacket, a rose-purple sleeveless jacket trimmed with two-toned gold-and-silver squirrel fur, and a scallion-yellow satin padded skirt. Everything was neither new nor old, and there was no impression of extravagance. Her lips were red without rouge, her brows dark without penciling; her face was like a silver basin and her eyes like moist apricot kernels. Because she seldom spoke, people said she hid her wisdom; content to adapt herself to circumstances, she called it keeping her limitations concealed. As Baoyu looked at her, he asked, “Cousin, are you quite recovered?” Baochai looked up and saw Baoyu enter. She quickly rose and replied with a smile, “I am almost entirely well now. It was kind of you to keep me in mind.” As she spoke, she invited him to sit on the edge of the kang and immediately told Ying'er to pour tea. At the same time, she asked after the health of the Old Lady and Lady Wang, and whether all the other girls were well. Meanwhile, she observed that Baoyu wore a purple-gold coronet of filigree set with jewels, a gold forehead band embroidered with two dragons contending for a pearl, an archer's jacket of incense-green satin embroidered with upright dragons and lined beneath the arms with white fox fur, and a five-colored sash patterned with butterflies and phoenixes. Around his neck hung a longevity lock and a name-registering talisman, as well as the piece of jade he had been born with in his mouth. Baochai smiled and said, “Everyone is forever talking about this jade of yours, but I have never examined it closely. Today I should like to have a look.” As she spoke, she moved closer. Baoyu also leaned toward her, removed the jade from his neck, and handed it to Baochai. Baochai held it on her palm and saw that it was as large as a sparrow's egg, radiant as the rosy clouds, smooth and lustrous as rich cream, and encircled by patterns in five colors. This was the illusory form assumed by that stubborn stone which had lain beneath Greensickness Peak in the Great Waste Mountains. A later poet once mocked it in these lines:

p.src: The Stone had also recorded this illusory form of his, together with the seal-script inscription carved by the scabby-headed monk, and its likeness is now reproduced below. Its actual form, however, was extremely small, small enough to be held in the mouth of an infant in the womb. Were it drawn to its true dimensions, the writing would be so minute that readers would severely strain their eyes, which would hardly be agreeable. Therefore, only its general form is followed here, with the proportions somewhat enlarged so that readers may examine it with ease by lamplight, even in their cups. This explanation is given so that no one may object: “How large could an unborn infant’s mouth be, and how could it possibly hold such a hulking, clumsy object?”

p.src: When Baochai had finished looking, she turned it back to the front and examined it closely, reciting, “Never lose, never forget; immortal life, eternal prosperity.” After repeating it twice, she turned to Ying'er and said with a smile, “Why are you standing there in a daze instead of going to pour the tea?” Ying'er giggled. “Those two phrases sound as though they make a pair with the two phrases on your necklace, miss.” Hearing this, Baoyu hastened to say with a smile, “So your necklace also bears eight characters, cousin. Let me admire them too.” “Do not listen to her,” said Baochai. “There are no characters on it.” Baoyu smilingly pleaded, “Dear cousin, I let you look at mine, did I not?” Unable to withstand his pestering, Baochai said, “Someone gave me two auspicious phrases, so they were engraved on it and I was told to wear it every day. Otherwise, what pleasure would there be in carrying such a heavy thing?” As she spoke, she undid the frogs and drew from over her bright-red inner jacket a glittering necklace of jewels and gleaming gold. p.src: Baoyu was now sitting close to Baochai and caught wave after wave of a cool, sweet, subtle fragrance, though he could not tell what scent it was. He therefore asked, “What incense have you perfumed yourself with, cousin? I have never smelled anything like it before.” Baochai smiled. “I detest incense. It makes perfectly good clothes reek of smoke and fire.” “Then what is this fragrance?” asked Baoyu. Baochai thought for a moment, then smiled. “Ah, yes—it must be the fragrance of the pills I took this morning.” Baoyu laughed. “What sort of pill smells so delightful? Dear cousin, give me one to taste.” Baochai laughed. “There you go fooling about again! Is medicine something to be swallowed indiscriminately?”

p.src: Before she had finished speaking, someone outside suddenly announced, “Miss Lin has arrived.” The words had scarcely been spoken when Lin Daiyu came swaying in. The moment she saw Baoyu, she smiled and exclaimed, “Oh dear, what an unfortunate time I have come!” Baoyu and the others hurriedly rose and smilingly invited her to sit. Baochai asked with a smile, “What makes you say that?” Daiyu smiled. “Had I known he was here, I would not have come.” “Now I understand you even less,” said Baochai. Daiyu smiled. “When people come, they all come together; when they stay away, not one of them comes. If he came today and I came tomorrow, and we took turns in this fashion, would you not have someone visiting you every day? Then things would be neither too lonely nor too lively. How is it that you do not understand, cousin?”

p.src: Seeing that Daiyu wore a bright-red, feather-satin, front-opening jacket over her clothes, Baoyu asked, “Has it begun to snow?” The old serving women below replied, “Snow pellets have been falling for half the day.” Baoyu asked, “Have they brought my cloak?” Daiyu immediately remarked, “There, you see? No sooner do I arrive than he must leave.” Baoyu laughed. “When did I ever say I was leaving? I only want it brought here in readiness.” Baoyu's nurse, Nanny Li, said, “It is snowing, and it is still early enough, so stay here and amuse yourself awhile with your elder and younger cousins. Your aunt is having tea and refreshments set out. I shall have a maid fetch your cloak and tell the young pages they may disperse.” Baoyu agreed. Nanny Li went out and dismissed all the pages, of whom nothing more need be said.

p.src: Meanwhile, Aunt Xue had set out several kinds of delicate tea cakes and fruit and invited them to take tea. Baoyu praised the fine goose feet and duck tongues he had eaten the other day at Cousin Zhen's residence. Hearing this, Aunt Xue promptly had some of her own wine-marinated delicacies brought for him to taste. Baoyu laughed. “These really ought to be eaten with wine.” Aunt Xue immediately ordered someone to pour out some of her finest wine. Nanny Li came forward and said, “Madam, perhaps we had better do without the wine.” Baoyu pleaded, “Nanny, I'll have only one cup.” “No, you cannot!” said Nanny Li. “In the presence of the Old Lady and your mother, you could drink a whole jar for all I care. That day I took my eyes off you for only a moment, and some ill-trained creature, eager only to win your favor and caring nothing for anyone else's fate, gave you a sip of wine—and I paid for it with two days of scolding. Madam does not know how troublesome his temper is; wine only makes him more headstrong. One day the Old Lady is in high spirits and lets him drink as much as he pleases, and another day she forbids it. Why should I be made to suffer for nothing?” Aunt Xue laughed. “You old fussbudget, go and enjoy your own food without worrying. I shall not let him drink too much. If the Old Lady asks, I shall answer for it.” Then she told a young maid, “Come, take the nannies away and give them a cup too, to ward off the chill.” After hearing this, Nanny Li had no choice but to go with the others for some wine and refreshments. Baoyu then said, “There is no need to warm it. I like my wine cold.” Aunt Xue hurriedly objected. “That will never do. Cold wine will make your hand tremble when you write.” Baochai laughed. “Cousin Bao, for all the miscellaneous learning you gather every day, can it be that you do not know wine is fiery by nature? If drunk warm, its heat disperses quickly; if drunk cold, it congeals inside, forcing the five organs to warm it. How could that fail to do you harm? From now on, you must stop drinking it cold.” Baoyu found her words reasonable, so he set down the cold wine and waited until it had been warmed before drinking.

p.src: Daiyu cracked melon seeds between her teeth, smiling with pursed lips. Just then Daiyu's young maid Xueyan arrived with a little hand warmer for her. Smiling, Daiyu asked, “Who told you to bring that? How thoughtful of her! As if I were about to freeze to death!” “Sister Zijuan was afraid you might be cold, miss, and sent me with it,” Xueyan replied. Daiyu took it and held it to her breast, laughing. “How good of you to obey her. Everything I tell you goes in one ear and out the other, yet the moment she speaks you obey, faster than if it were an imperial decree!” Hearing this, Baoyu knew Daiyu was using the occasion to mock him. Having no answer, he merely gave a couple of sheepish chuckles. Baochai had long been accustomed to Daiyu's ways and paid her no attention. Aunt Xue said, “You have always been delicate and cannot bear the cold. Is it wrong of them to be concerned about you?” Daiyu laughed. “You do not understand, Aunt. Fortunately, I am here with you. If we were in someone else's home, would our hosts not be offended? It would look as if we had noticed that our hosts could not even provide a hand warmer and had specially sent home for one. Instead of blaming my maids for being overanxious, people might think I had always been accustomed to behaving with such thoughtless presumption.” Aunt Xue replied, “What a worrier you are! You may think so, but I certainly do not.”

Aunt Xue said, “You have always been delicate and cannot bear the cold. Is it wrong of them to be concerned about you?”
Daiyu laughed. “You do not understand, Aunt.
Fortunately, I am here with you. If we were in someone else's home, would our hosts not be offended?
It would look as if we had noticed that our hosts could not even provide a hand warmer and had specially sent home for one.
Instead of blaming my maids for being overanxious, people might think I had always been accustomed to behaving with such thoughtless presumption.”
Aunt Xue replied, “What a worrier you are! You may think so, but I certainly do not.”

p.src: While they were talking, Baoyu had already finished three cups. Nanny Li came forward once more to stop him. But Baoyu, thoroughly content as he laughed and chatted with Baochai and Daiyu, had no intention of giving up his wine. He had no choice but to plead humbly, “Dear Nanny, let me have just two more cups, and then I shall stop.” Nanny Li said, “You had better remember that your father is at home today. Take care in case he questions you about your lessons!” At these words Baoyu became deeply uneasy. He slowly put down his cup and bowed his head. Daiyu hastily spoke first. “Do not spoil everyone's pleasure! If your uncle sends for you, we shall simply say your aunt kept you here. This nanny has had some wine herself, and now she is making us the target of her ill humor!” As she spoke, she secretly nudged Baoyu to provoke his defiance and muttered under her breath, “Pay no attention to that old thing. Let us go on enjoying ourselves.” Nanny Li did not understand Daiyu's intention and said, “Miss Lin, you must not encourage him. You should persuade him instead; he might listen to you.” Lin Daiyu sneered. “Why should I encourage him? Nor is it my place to advise him. You are far too cautious, Nanny. The Old Lady often gives him wine; surely one extra sip here at Aunt's can do no harm. Unless, perhaps, Aunt's household consists of outsiders and he ought not to be here at all.” Nanny Li was both flustered and amused. “Really, Miss Lin, every word you utter is sharper than a knife. What could you possibly mean by that?” Baochai could no longer suppress her laughter. She pinched Daiyu's cheek and said, “That sharp-tongued Miss Frowner! One can neither hate you nor bring oneself simply to like you.” Meanwhile Aunt Xue said, “Do not be afraid, do not be afraid, my dear boy! I have nothing fine to offer you here, so do not let this paltry fare frighten you into brooding over it; that would only make me uneasy. Eat and drink without a care. I shall take responsibility for everything. Stay and have dinner as well; if you get drunk, you can simply sleep here with me.” Then she ordered, “Bring some more wine and heat it well! Your aunt will drink two cups with you, and then we shall have dinner.” Only then did Baoyu recover his spirits.

p.src: Nanny Li instructed the young maids, “Keep a careful eye on him here. I shall go home, change my clothes, and return. Quietly tell Her Ladyship not to indulge him or let him drink too much.” With that, she went home. Although two or three older serving women remained, none of them felt responsible; once Nanny Li had gone, they too quietly slipped away on errands of their own. Only two young maids were left, delighted at the chance to please Baoyu. Fortunately, Aunt Xue coaxed and cajoled him until he agreed to drink only a few cups, whereupon she hurriedly had the wine removed. She had sour-bamboo-shoot and chicken-skin soup prepared; Baoyu drank two bowls heartily and ate half a bowl of fine greenish rice congee. Presently Baochai and Daiyu also finished their meal, and strong tea was brewed for everyone. Only then did Aunt Xue set her mind at ease. Xueyan and three or four other maids, having eaten their meal, came in to attend them. Daiyu asked Baoyu, “Are you leaving or not?” Baoyu replied through bleary, weary eyes, “If you are leaving, I shall go with you.” At this, Daiyu rose and said, “We have been here the whole day; it is time we went back. Who knows how they may be looking for us over there?” With that, the two took their leave.

p.src: A young maid hurriedly brought over Baoyu’s hood. He dipped his head slightly and told her to put it on him. The maid gave the bright-red felt hood a shake and had only just fitted it over his head when Baoyu cried, “Enough, enough! You clumsy thing, be gentler! Have you never seen anyone wear one before? Let me put it on myself.” Standing at the edge of the kang, Daiyu said, “Why make such a fuss? Come here and let me see to it.” Baoyu hurried over to her. Daiyu adjusted it with her hands, gently fitting it over his hair-binding crown and tucking its brim above his forehead band. Then she raised the walnut-sized tasselled pin of crimson floss so that it trembled outside the hood. When she had finished, she looked him over and said, “There, that will do. Now put on your cloak.” Only then did Baoyu take the cloak and put it on. Aunt Xue hastened to say, “Your nurses have not returned yet. There is no harm in waiting a little longer.” Baoyu said, “We can go and wait for them instead. The maids with us will be enough.” Still uneasy, Aunt Xue insisted on sending two serving women to accompany the young cousins. The two thanked her for her hospitality and went straight back to Grandmother Jia’s apartments.

p.src: Grandmother Jia had not yet eaten her evening meal, and when she learned that they had come from Aunt Xue’s, she was all the more pleased. Seeing that Baoyu had been drinking, she ordered him to return to his room and rest, forbidding him to come out again. She also ordered the servants to take good care of him. Suddenly remembering Baoyu’s attendants, she asked everyone, “Where is Nanny Li? Why do I not see her?” No one dared say outright that she had gone home, so they merely replied, “She came in just now but must have gone off on some errand.” Baoyu turned around unsteadily and said, “She enjoys an easier life than even Grandmother does. Why ask after her? Without her, I might even live a couple of days longer.” As he spoke, he made his way to his own bedroom. There were brush and ink on the desk. Qingwen came forward to meet him and said with a laugh, “Very good, very good! You had me grind all that ink, and in your fine spirits this morning you wrote only three characters before throwing down your brush and leaving, keeping us waiting all day. Come quickly and use up the rest of this ink for me!” Baoyu suddenly remembered what had happened that morning and asked with a smile, “Where are those three characters I wrote?” Qingwen laughed. “Now here is someone truly drunk! Before you went over to the other mansion, you told us to paste them above this doorway, and now you ask where they are. I was afraid someone else might paste them crooked, so I climbed a ladder and put them up myself. Even now my hands are still frozen stiff.” Baoyu laughed. “I forgot. If your hands are cold, I shall warm them for you.” With that, he reached out and took Qingwen’s hand, and together they raised their heads to look at the three newly inscribed characters above the doorway.

p.src: Presently Daiyu arrived. Baoyu said with a smile, “Dear cousin, tell me honestly: which one of these three characters is well written?” Daiyu looked up above the inner-room doorway, where three newly pasted characters read “Crimson-Cloud Studio.” Daiyu laughed. “Every one of them is good. How did you come to write so beautifully? Tomorrow you must write a signboard for me too.” Baoyu giggled and said, “You are teasing me again.” Then he asked, “Where is Sister Xiren?” Qingwen pursed her lips toward the kang in the inner room. Baoyu looked and saw Xiren lying there asleep, still fully dressed. Baoyu laughed. “Well, she has gone to warm herself rather early.” Then he asked Qingwen, “When I had breakfast at the other mansion today, there was a plate of bean-curd-skin buns. I remembered how fond you are of them, so I told Mistress Zhen that I was saving them for supper and had someone bring them over. Did you eat them?” “Do not even mention them,” Qingwen replied. As soon as they arrived, I knew they were for me; but I had only just eaten, so I left them there. Later Nanny Li came, saw them, and said, ‘Baoyu probably will not eat these. Let me take them home for my grandson.’ Then she had someone take them to her home.” Just then Qianxue came forward carrying tea. Baoyu offered it, saying, “Cousin Lin, have some tea.” Everyone laughed and said, “Cousin Lin left long ago, and you are still offering her tea!”

p.src: After drinking half a bowl of tea, Baoyu suddenly remembered the tea from that morning and asked Qianxue, “A bowl of Maple Dew tea was brewed this morning. I told you that the tea only reaches its finest after being steeped three or four times, so why have you brewed this instead?” Qianxue replied, “I had saved it, but when Nanny Li came, she wanted a taste, so I gave it to her.” At this, Baoyu casually flung the teacup in his hand to the floor. It shattered with a crash, splashing tea all over Qianxue’s skirt. Then he sprang to his feet and demanded of Qianxue, “What sort of grandmother is she to you that you all show her such devotion? She merely relies on having nursed me for a few days when I was little. Now she carries on as though she were greater than our ancestors. I have no need of her milk now, so why should we maintain this ancestor for nothing? Throw her out, and we shall all be rid of the nuisance!” With that, he made to report immediately to Grandmother Jia and have his wet nurse expelled. In truth, Xiren had not been asleep at all. She had only pretended to sleep so that Baoyu would come and tease her in play. At first, when she heard him discussing written characters and asking about the buns and such matters, she saw no need to rise; but when he smashed the teacup and lost his temper, she hurriedly got up to explain matters and restrain him. Grandmother Jia had already sent someone to ask what had happened. Xiren hastily said, “I was bringing tea just now when I slipped on the snow and dropped the cup.” At the same time, she soothed Baoyu, saying, “If you are determined to drive her out, very well. All of us are willing to leave too. You may as well take this opportunity to drive us all out together. That will suit us, and you need not worry that no better servants will come to attend you.” Only after hearing this did Baoyu fall silent. Xiren and the others helped him onto the kang and changed his clothes. No one could tell what Baoyu was still muttering, for his speech was slurred and his eyelids grew ever heavier. They hurriedly attended him and put him to bed. Xiren reached out and removed the Jade of Spiritual Understanding from his neck, wrapped it in her own handkerchief, and tucked it beneath the mattress so that it would not feel cold against his neck when he put it on the next day. As soon as Baoyu laid his head on the pillow, he fell asleep. By then Nanny Li and the others had already come in. Hearing that Baoyu was drunk, they dared not approach and risk offending him further. They merely made quiet inquiries, and only after learning that he was asleep did they feel relieved and disperse.

p.src: When Baoyu awoke the next day, someone reported, “Young Master Rong has brought young Mr. Qin to pay a call.” Baoyu hurried out to receive them and led them in to pay their respects to Grandmother Jia. Grandmother Jia saw that Qin Zhong was handsome in appearance and gentle in manner, and judged him a suitable companion for Baoyu’s studies. She was delighted, kept him for tea and a meal, and then ordered someone to take him to meet Lady Wang and the others. Since everyone had always been fond of Lady Qin, they were pleased to find Qin Zhong such a fine young man, and each gave him a parting gift when he left. Grandmother Jia also gave him a purse and a golden image of Kui, the Star of Literature, symbolizing the auspicious union of literary stars. She also instructed him, “Your home is far away. If at any time the weather, your health, or your meals make things inconvenient, you may simply stay here as long as you wish. Just stay with your Uncle Bao, and do not follow those good-for-nothing fellows or learn their ways.” Qin Zhong agreed to everything and went home to report it.

p.src: His father, Qin Ye, then held the office of Director in the Imperial Works Department. He was nearly seventy, and his wife had died long before. Having had no children in earlier years, he had adopted a boy and a girl from the Foundling Home. The boy, however, died, leaving only the girl, whose childhood name was Ke’er. As she grew up, she became graceful in appearance and charming in disposition. Because Qin Ye had certain connections with the Jia family, the two families formed a marriage alliance, and she was betrothed to Jia Rong. Qin Ye did not have Qin Zhong until he was past fifty. As the boy’s tutor had died the previous year and Qin Ye had not yet found time to engage another capable teacher, Qin Zhong could only review his former lessons at home for the time being. Qin Ye had been thinking of consulting his relatives by marriage and sending Qin Zhong to their family school so that his studies would not be neglected. Just then, this opportunity arose through Baoyu. He also knew that the Jia family school was currently supervised by Jia Dairu, an eminent scholar of the old school. Qin Zhong’s studies would surely advance under him, and he might even hope to make a name for himself. Qin Ye was therefore greatly delighted. His official purse, however, was meager, while everyone in the Jia household, high and low, judged others by their wealth and rank; it would not do to appear empty-handed. For the sake of his son’s future, Qin Ye had no choice but to scrape together twenty-four taels from every possible source, seal them respectfully as an introductory gift, and personally take Qin Zhong to call upon Jia Dairu. After that, they would wait until the day Baoyu began school, so that the two boys might enter together. Indeed:
